title: Retry policy with capped exponential backoff and full jitter
prompt:
Implement `src/index.js` so it exports `PolicyError`, `normalizePolicy`, `classifyError`, `computeSchedule` and `planAttempts`. Everything is pure: no timers, no clock, no I/O. `PolicyError` extends `Error`, sets `name` to `'PolicyError'`, and carries a `code` string; its constructor takes `(code, message)`.

`normalizePolicy(input)` validates a raw configuration and returns a frozen object with exactly the keys `baseMs`, `maxAttempts`, `factor`, `maxDelayMs`, `budgetMs` and `jitter`. `baseMs` and `maxAttempts` are required integers of at least 1. `factor` defaults to 2 and must be a finite number of at least 1. `maxDelayMs` defaults to 30000 and must be an integer of at least 1. `budgetMs` defaults to `Infinity` and must be either `Infinity` or an integer of at least 0. `jitter` defaults to `'full'` and must be `'full'` or `'none'`. A field present with the value `undefined` counts as absent. Checks run in this order and the first failure throws: the input must be a non-null, non-array object (`code` `'INVALID_POLICY'`, message `policy must be an object`); every own key must be one of the six known names, checked in `Object.keys` order (`'UNKNOWN_FIELD'`, `unknown policy field: <key>`); then `baseMs` and `maxAttempts` in that order (`'MISSING_FIELD'`, `missing required policy field: <name>`, or `'INVALID_FIELD'`, `invalid policy field: <name>`); then `factor`, `maxDelayMs`, `budgetMs` and `jitter` in that order (`'INVALID_FIELD'` with the same message form).

`classifyError(error)` returns `'retryable'` or `'permanent'`. Anything that is not a non-null object is permanent. An explicit boolean `retryable` property decides on its own and outranks everything else. Otherwise, if `status` is an integer, it alone decides: 501 is permanent, 408 and 429 are retryable, 500 through 599 are retryable, and every other integer status is permanent. A `status` that is not an integer (including `NaN` and fractional numbers) is ignored, and classification falls through to `code`: a string `code` matching, case-insensitively, one of `ETIMEDOUT`, `ECONNRESET`, `ECONNREFUSED`, `EAI_AGAIN`, `EPIPE` or `ENETUNREACH` is retryable. Anything else is permanent.

`computeSchedule(policy, random)` normalizes `policy` (so invalid configuration still throws) and requires `random` to be a function returning values in [0, 1), throwing `'INVALID_RANDOM'` with message `random must be a function` otherwise. A policy allowing `maxAttempts` attempts has at most `maxAttempts - 1` retry slots, numbered from 1. The uncapped delay for slot `n` is `baseMs * factor ** (n - 1)`; the capped delay is that value clamped to `maxDelayMs` and then floored to an integer. Under `jitter: 'none'` the delay is the capped value and `random` is never called; under `'full'` each slot draws exactly one value `r` from `random()` and the delay is `Math.floor(r * (capped + 1))`. Slots are processed in order, and the draw for a slot happens before the budget is examined, so a slot the budget rejects still consumes a draw. If adding a slot's delay would make the running total exceed `budgetMs`, that slot and every later slot are dropped. The return value is `{ delays, totalDelayMs, stopReason }`, where `stopReason` is `'budget'` when a slot was dropped and `'attempts'` when the schedule ran out of slots first.

`planAttempts(policy, outcomes, random)` replays a call against a fixed list of outcomes. Each outcome is `{ ok: true, value }` or `{ ok: false, error }`; `outcomes` must be a non-empty array (`'INVALID_OUTCOMES'`, `outcomes must be a non-empty array`) and every element must be a non-null object with a boolean `ok` (`'INVALID_OUTCOMES'`, `outcome <index> must have a boolean ok field`), both validated before any attempt is simulated. Attempt `n` consumes `outcomes[n - 1]`; running past the end throws `'OUTCOMES_EXHAUSTED'` with message `outcome sequence exhausted`. A successful outcome returns `{ status: 'succeeded', attempts, value, waits, totalDelayMs }`. A failure returns `{ status: 'failed', reason, error, attempts, waits, totalDelayMs }` with `reason` `'permanent'` when the error is not retryable, `'attempts'` when no attempt is left, and `'budget'` when the next wait would overrun the budget. Otherwise the run takes retry slot `n` after attempt `n`, drawing and budgeting exactly as `computeSchedule` does, appends the delay to `waits` and continues, so a run of nothing but retryable failures produces the same waits as the schedule built from the same policy and random stream.
